explain.es: La nominalización consiste en expresar como sustantivo lo que normalmente diríamos con un verbo o un adjetivo: analyse → analysis, fail → failure, accurate → accuracy. Cuando convertimos una oración entera en una frase nominal (because prices rose → owing to the rise in prices), el texto se vuelve más denso, más impersonal y más abstracto: es el sello del inglés académico, jurídico, científico y de la prensa de calidad. En español ocurre lo mismo («tras la aprobación de la ley»), pero los sufijos, las colocaciones y las preposiciones del inglés son otros, y ahí está la dificultad.
explain.en: Nominalisation means expressing actions and qualities as nouns. Turning clauses into noun phrases makes writing denser, more impersonal and more abstract: the hallmark of academic, legal and scientific English.

explain.title: 1 · De verbo a sustantivo
explain.es: La mayoría de los verbos forman su sustantivo con un sufijo. Los más productivos son -tion/-sion (reduce → reduction, decide → decision), -ment (achieve → achievement), -ance/-ence (comply → compliance, refer → reference), -al (refuse → refusal, approve → approval), -ure (fail → failure, disclose → disclosure) y -sis, de origen griego (analyse → analysis, emphasise → emphasis). Ojo: el sufijo no es predecible y a menudo no coincide con el español; hay que aprender cada sustantivo (refusal, nunca refusement).
explain.en: Most verbs take a suffix: -tion/-sion, -ment, -ance/-ence, -al, -ure, -sis. The suffix is not predictable, so learn each noun individually.

examples.en: The reduction of emissions is a global priority.
examples.es: La reducción de las emisiones es una prioridad mundial.
Su negativa a hacer declaraciones alimentó las especulaciones.

examples.en: The failure of the talks surprised nobody.
examples.es: El fracaso de las negociaciones no sorprendió a nadie.

explain.title: 2 · De adjetivo a sustantivo
explain.es: Las cualidades también se convierten en sustantivos abstractos: -ity (complex → complexity, scarce → scarcity, feasible → feasibility), -ness (aware → awareness, effective → effectiveness), -ance/-ence (relevant → relevance, reluctant → reluctance), -cy (accurate → accuracy, efficient → efficiency) y -th, con cambio vocálico (long → length, strong → strength, wide → width, deep → depth, true → truth). Al nominalizar, el adverbio que modificaba al adjetivo pasa a ser adjetivo: extremely complex → extreme complexity.
explain.en: Qualities become abstract nouns: -ity, -ness, -ance/-ence, -cy, -th. Any adverb becomes an adjective: extremely complex → extreme complexity.

examples.en: The complexity of the task was underestimated.
examples.es: Se subestimó la complejidad de la tarea.

examples.en: There is growing awareness of the risks.
examples.es: Hay una conciencia cada vez mayor de los riesgos.

examples.en: The length of the report discouraged many readers.
examples.es: La extensión del informe desanimó a muchos lectores.

explain.title: 3 · Conversión: misma forma, otro acento
explain.es: Muchos verbos funcionan también como sustantivo sin cambiar de forma: increase, decrease, decline, rise, fall, change, review, demand, delay, report, release. En prosa formal se combinan con un adjetivo y una preposición fija: a sharp rise in, a steady decline in, a thorough review of. En varios bisílabos cambia el acento: el verbo lo lleva en la 2.ª sílaba (to inCREASE, to reCORD, to imPORT) y el sustantivo en la 1.ª (an INcrease, a REcord, an IMport).
explain.en: Many verbs are also nouns with no change: increase, decline, review. Typical pattern: adjective + noun + fixed preposition (a sharp rise in). Two-syllable pairs often shift stress: to inCREASE / an INcrease.

examples.en: There has been a sharp rise in energy prices.
examples.es: Ha habido una fuerte subida de los precios de la energía.

examples.en: The board ordered a thorough review of safety procedures.
examples.es: La junta ordenó una revisión exhaustiva de los procedimientos de seguridad.

examples.en: The decline in birth rates is reshaping Europe.
examples.es: El descenso de la natalidad está transformando Europa.

explain.title: 4 · De oración a frase nominal
explain.es: Este es el paso clave del estilo académico. Para condensar una oración en una frase nominal: (1) el verbo se convierte en sustantivo; (2) el adverbio pasa a adjetivo; (3) el sujeto pasa a genitivo (the government's), a frase con of/by o a adjetivo (economic); (4) el objeto va con of; (5) la conjunción se sustituye por una preposición: because → owing to, although → despite, after → following, when → upon. Resultado: una sola oración principal que contiene mucha más información.
explain.en: To condense a clause: verb → noun, adverb → adjective, subject → possessive / of-phrase / adjective, object → of + noun, conjunction → preposition.
formula: owing to + *the rapid growth of the economy*

examples.en: Owing to rapid economic growth, unemployment fell.
examples.es: Debido al rápido crecimiento económico, el paro descendió.

examples.en: Following the minister's resignation, the party collapsed in the polls.
examples.es: Tras la dimisión del ministro, el partido se hundió en las encuestas.

examples.en: Despite the scarcity of evidence, the theory gained acceptance.
examples.es: Pese a la escasez de pruebas, la teoría fue ganando aceptación.

explain.title: 5 · Verbos que encadenan sustantivos
explain.es: Una vez nominalizadas las ideas, las unimos con verbos de causa-efecto. Fíjate en la dirección: CAUSA leads to / results in / gives rise to / brings about / contributes to / triggers EFECTO, pero EFECTO results from / stems from / arises from / is attributable to CAUSA. Result in y result from significan lo contrario: es un error frecuentísimo incluso en niveles altos. Con estos verbos la lógica del texto queda clarísima: A → B en una sola cláusula.
explain.en: Link nominalised ideas with cause–effect verbs. CAUSE leads to / results in / gives rise to EFFECT; EFFECT results from / stems from / arises from CAUSE.
formula: CAUSA + *lead to / result in / give rise to* + EFECTO
EFECTO + *result from / stem from / arise from* + CAUSA

explain.title: Mapa de sufijos
head: Sufijo · Suffix
Base
Sustantivo · Noun
En contexto · In context
rows: an increase, a decline, a review
explain.note: Plurales griegos: analysis → analyses, hypothesis → hypotheses, crisis → crises, basis → bases. Y hay sustantivos irregulares que conviene memorizar: deny → denial, die → death, choose → choice, prove → proof, believe → belief.
explain.note_en: Greek plurals: analyses, hypotheses, crises, bases. Some nouns are irregular: denial, death, choice, proof, belief.

explain.title: Conectores: de conjunción a preposición
head: Relación · Meaning
Con oración (informal)
Con sustantivo (formal)
Ejemplo · Example
rows: owing to, due to, in view of, on account of
In view of the costs, the plan was dropped.
Despite its flaws, the study is valuable.
Prior to publication, the data were checked.
in the event of, in the absence of
In the event of fire, use the stairs.
with a view to, for the purpose of
talks with a view to a ceasefire
In contrast to its rivals, the firm grew.
explain.note: Due to se usa tradicionalmente tras be (The delay was due to the strike); a principio de frase el registro esmerado prefiere owing to. Si necesitas una oración completa tras la preposición, añade the fact that: owing to the fact that…, despite the fact that…
explain.note_en: Traditionally due to follows be; owing to is preferred at the start of a sentence. Need a full clause? Add the fact that.

explain.title: 6 · La frase nominal compleja
explain.es: El inglés académico acumula información antes del sustantivo (premodificación: a rapid increase, government policy, long-term unemployment) y después (posmodificación con of, in, for… o con una relativa). Dos consejos: (1) cuando el modificador es breve, prefiere el genitivo o un sustantivo en función de adjetivo a las cadenas de of: the impact of the reform of the system of pensions → the impact of pension reform; (2) no amontones más de tres sustantivos seguidos: the student housing allocation policy review resulta opaco.
explain.en: Pack information before the noun (adjectives, noun modifiers) and after it (prepositional phrases). Avoid long chains of of and stacks of more than three nouns.

examples.en: The rapid expansion of renewable energy has cut emissions.
examples.es: La rápida expansión de las energías renovables ha reducido las emisiones.
El paro de larga duración sigue siendo un grave problema.

examples.en: The impact of pension reform on young workers is unclear.
examples.es: No está claro el impacto de la reforma de las pensiones en los trabajadores jóvenes.

explain.title: Estilo verbal frente a estilo nominal
explain.es: Mismo contenido, dos registros. El estilo verbal es más directo y fácil de leer; el nominal es más compacto e impersonal, propio de informes, artículos y textos jurídicos.
explain.en: Same content, two registers: verbal style is direct; nominal style is compact and impersonal.

explain.title: Un texto, dos versiones: densidad léxica
explain.title_en: One text, two versions: lexical density
explain.es: La densidad léxica es la proporción de palabras con contenido (sustantivos, verbos léxicos, adjetivos y adverbios) respecto al total. La versión académica dice lo mismo con menos palabras, menos verbos conjugados y más sustantivos: cada frase nominal «empaqueta» una oración entera.
explain.en: Lexical density = content words ÷ total words. The academic version says the same with fewer words, fewer finite verbs and more nouns.

items.why: «Realizar un estudio» no es realise (= darse cuenta). Usa carry out, conduct, undertake.
items.why_en: Realise = become aware. Use carry out / conduct / undertake.

items.why: Increasement no existe: increase es verbo y sustantivo (conversión). Igual: refusal, no refusement.
items.why_en: Increase is both verb and noun. Likewise refusal, not refusement.

items.bad: <s>The</s> education is the key to <s>the</s> progress.
items.why: Los sustantivos abstractos en sentido general van sin artículo: society, education, technology, progress.
items.why_en: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article.

items.why: El sustantivo hereda el complemento del verbo: decide to → decision to; refuse to → refusal to; fail to → failure to.
items.why_en: Nouns keep their verb's pattern: decision / refusal / failure + to-infinitive.

items.bad: <s>Owing to the economy grew</s>, unemployment fell.
items.why: Owing to, due to, despite, following son preposiciones: van con sustantivo, no con oración (o bien con the fact that).
items.why_en: These are prepositions: noun phrase, not clause.

items.why: result in = provocar (causa → efecto); result from = deberse a (efecto ← causa).
items.why_en: result in = cause; result from = be caused by.

items.why: El sustantivo de «subida» es rise (de rise, intransitivo); raise es transitivo: to raise prices. En BrE: a pay rise.
items.why_en: A rise in prices; to raise prices; BrE a pay rise.

items.bad: <s>The making of a decision on the implementation of the plan was carried out by the board.</s>
items.good: The board decided to implement the plan.
items.why: Sobrenominalización (zombie nouns): si la frase nominal no aporta nada, vuelve al verbo.
items.why_en: Over-nominalisation: use the verb when nouns add nothing.

explain.title: Registro: ¿cuándo NO nominalizar?
explain.es: La nominalización es propia de artículos científicos, informes, textos jurídicos y prensa de calidad. En correos, presentaciones orales o textos divulgativos, el exceso suena pomposo u opaco: la especialista en escritura académica Helen Sword llama a estos sustantivos vacíos zombie nouns. Regla práctica: nominaliza para empaquetar un concepto que vas a retomar (this reduction…, such a decline…), no para esconder quién hizo qué. Y no sustituyas un verbo claro por make + sustantivo sin motivo: make an assessment of → assess.
explain.en: Nominalise to package a concept you will build on, not to hide who did what. In emails and speech, prefer verbs and avoid 'zombie nouns'.

explain.title: ¿Cómo nominalizo una frase?
explain.title_en: How do I nominalise a sentence?

items.es: Localiza el verbo o el adjetivo que expresa la idea clave: The economy grew rapidly because exports increased.
items.en: Find the key verb or adjective.

items.es: Busca su sustantivo (sufijo o conversión) y comprueba que existe: grow → growth, increase → increase.
items.en: Find the noun form and check that it exists.

items.es: Convierte el adverbio en adjetivo y el sujeto/objeto en genitivo, frase con of o modificador: rapid economic growth, an increase in exports.
items.en: Adverb → adjective; subject/object → possessive, of-phrase or modifier.

items.es: Sustituye la conjunción por una preposición (because → owing to) o enlaza con un verbo de causa-efecto (lead to, result in).
items.en: Replace the conjunction with a preposition or a cause–effect verb.

items.es: Ensambla la frase: An increase in exports led to rapid economic growth.
items.en: Assemble: An increase in exports led to rapid economic growth.

items.es: Relee: ¿se entiende mejor? ¿Se ha perdido quién hizo qué? Si no ganas nada, <mark>vuelve al verbo</mark>.
items.en: Reread: is it clearer? If not, go back to the verb.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T (verdadero) o F (falso) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Anyone who has read a scientific journal will have noticed a peculiar feature of academic prose: its fondness for nouns. Where a journalist might write that scientists tested the vaccine and found that it worked, a researcher is more likely to report the evaluation of the vaccine's efficacy. The linguist M.A.K. Halliday described this shift from verbs to nouns as a form of grammatical metaphor: processes and qualities are repackaged as things.

The advantages are considerable. Nominalisation allows writers to compress a great deal of information into a single phrase, to present an earlier argument as a given (this reduction, such a decline) and to build long chains of reasoning in which one noun phrase becomes the subject of the next sentence. It also lends prose an air of objectivity, since the people who performed the actions tend to disappear.

That disappearance, however, is precisely what worries critics. The writing scholar Helen Sword has called excessive nominalisations zombie nouns because they suck the life out of sentences: the implementation of the reorganisation of the department is far harder to process than they reorganised the department. Strings of abstract nouns can also conceal responsibility, as in mistakes were made in the allocation of funds. Good academic writers, then, nominalise selectively: when a noun phrase packages a key concept, they use it; when it merely obscures who did what, they return to a verb.

items.q: According to the text, journalists use more nouns than researchers.
items.why: Researchers are more likely to use nominal style.

items.q: Halliday regarded nominalisation as a type of grammatical metaphor.
Nominalisation makes it easier to identify who performed an action.
items.why: The people who performed the actions tend to disappear.

items.q: Helen Sword recommends avoiding nouns altogether.
items.why: She criticises excessive nominalisations, not nouns in general.

items.q: Give two advantages of nominalisation mentioned in the text.
items.a: Any two: compressing information; presenting earlier arguments as given; building chains of reasoning; objectivity.

items.q: Why are excessive nominalisations called zombie nouns?
items.a: Because they suck the life out of sentences and make them harder to process.

items.q: Which noun phrase in paragraph 1 corresponds to tested the vaccine and found that it worked?
items.a: the evaluation of the vaccine's efficacy

items.q: Rewrite mistakes were made in the allocation of funds with an active verb and a clear agent.
items.a: e.g. The committee allocated the funds incorrectly.

items.q: According to the last paragraph, when do good writers return to a verb?
items.a: When a noun phrase merely obscures who did what.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe en estilo académico. Usa nominalizaciones, colocaciones formales y verbos de causa-efecto.
exercises.en: Write in academic style using nominalisation.

items.q: Reescribe en estilo académico (máx. 35 palabras): «Because lots of tourists come to the city, rents have gone up and local people can't afford to live in the centre any more.»
items.a: Ej.: The massive influx of tourists into the city has led to a sharp rise in rents, which has priced many local residents out of the historic centre.

items.q: Escribe dos frases sobre un problema de tu ciudad: una con lead to / result in y otra con stem from.
items.a: Ej.: The lack of reliable public transport inevitably leads to heavy traffic congestion in the city centre at peak times. Much of the air pollution stems from the widespread use of private cars.

items.q: Escribe una frase con owing to, otra con despite y otra con upon + sustantivo.
items.a: Ej.: Owing to the strike, all flights were cancelled. Despite the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned. Upon arrival, all guests receive a welcome pack and a map of the city.

items.q: Escribe un breve abstract (40-60 palabras) de un estudio imaginario con al menos cinco nominalizaciones y dos colocaciones formales (carry out, reach…).
items.a: Ej.: This study examines the impact of remote working on employee well-being. A survey was carried out among 1,200 workers. Analysis of the data revealed a significant reduction in stress but a marked increase in feelings of isolation, pointing to the need for a balanced approach to hybrid working.

checklist.es: Formo el sustantivo correcto de verbos y adjetivos (refusal, failure, scarcity, width).
checklist.en: I can form the correct noun from verbs and adjectives.

checklist.es: Transformo una oración en frase nominal: verbo → sustantivo, adverbio → adjetivo.
checklist.en: I can turn a clause into a noun phrase.

checklist.es: Sustituyo conjunciones por preposiciones: owing to, despite, following, upon.
checklist.en: I can replace conjunctions with prepositions.

checklist.es: Uso bien lead to / result in / stem from sin confundir la dirección causa-efecto.
checklist.en: I use cause–effect verbs in the right direction.

checklist.es: Domino colocaciones formales: carry out, conduct, reach, pose, draw.
checklist.en: I know formal collocations such as carry out an investigation.

checklist.es: Sé cuándo NO nominalizar y evito los zombie nouns.
checklist.en: I know when not to nominalise and avoid zombie nouns.
